cards.text: Welcome back, friend. Abimelech has now reigned over Israel for three years, and the leaders of Shechem are the ones who put him there. Everything looks settled, but it isn't.

cards.question: Three years in, God sends something between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem. What is it?

cards.text: Now the leaders of Shechem start treating Abimelech deceitfully. And the text tells us exactly why God did this.

cards.question: Why does God send that spirit between Abimelech and the leaders of Shechem?

answers.text: So justice comes for the seventy sons
So Israel turns back to the LORD
So Midian stays out of the land

cards.question: Abimelech is the only one who will answer for the murder of the seventy sons of Jerubbaal.

cards.text: The leaders of Shechem set up an ambush against Abimelech on the hilltops, and they rob everybody who passes by on the road. That's not an ambush, friend. That's a toll booth with an attitude.

cards.question: The leaders of Shechem are robbing everyone on the road. What happens to the news of it?

answers.text: It stays a secret in Shechem
It reaches Jotham in Beer first

cards.text: Meanwhile, Gaal son of Ebed rolls into Shechem with his brothers, and the leaders of Shechem put their confidence in him. Three years with one king, and they're already checking out the new guy.
Harvest time. They gather the grapes, tread them, hold a festival and go into the house of their god.

cards.question: As they ate and drank in the house of their god, the people of Shechem ___ Abimelech.

cards.text: Then Gaal stands up and says, "Who is Abimelech, and who is Shechem, that we should serve him?" Oh, he is just getting warmed up.

cards.question: Gaal wishes the people of Shechem were under his authority. What does he say he would do with Abimelech?

cards.text: Big talk. Gaal is the guy in the group chat who's DEFINITELY gonna say something to the boss. But Zebul, the governor of the city and Abimelech's officer, hears every word, and he burns with anger.

cards.question: Zebul secretly sends messengers to warn Abimelech that Gaal is stirring up the city against him.
Zebul's message also gives Abimelech a plan. What is it?

answers.text: Lie in wait tonight and attack at sunrise
March in at noon with trumpets blowing
Stay away until Gaal leaves the city

cards.text: Abimelech and his troops set out by night and lie in wait against Shechem in four companies. In the morning, Gaal goes out to the city gate just as they come out of hiding.

cards.question: Gaal points and tells Zebul that people are coming down from the mountains. What does Zebul say back?

answers.text: The shadows of the mountains look like men to you
Those are only shepherds bringing in their flocks
That is the army you sent for yourself

cards.text: Gaal looks again: people coming from the center of the land, plus a company coming by way of the Diviners' Oak. Friend, those are some VERY organized shadows.

cards.question: Zebul drops the act and reminds Gaal of his big talk. Then he says, "Go out now and ___ them!"
Gaal leads the leaders of Shechem out against Abimelech and wins the day.

cards.text: Round one is over. Abimelech stays in Arumah, and Zebul drives Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem. All that big talk, and Gaal didn't even get to unpack.

cards.question: The next day the people of Shechem go out into the fields, and Abimelech hears about it. What does he do?

answers.text: Lies in wait and attacks them
Sends them a message of peace

cards.question: This time Abimelech divides his men into three companies.

cards.text: Abimelech's company takes its stand at the city gate, while the other two strike down everyone in the fields. All that day he fights until he captures the city and kills its people.

cards.question: After capturing Shechem, Abimelech demolished the city and sowed it with ___.

cards.text: The leaders in the tower of Shechem hear what happened and go into the inner chamber of the temple of El-berith. Then somebody tells Abimelech they're all gathered there.

cards.question: Abimelech and his men go up Mount Zalmon, and he takes his axe in his hand. What does he cut?
With the branch on his shoulder, Abimelech tells his men to hurry and do what they've seen him do.

cards.text: Each man cuts his own branch and follows Abimelech. They pile the branches against the inner chamber and set it on fire above them.

cards.question: How many people die in the tower of Shechem?

answers.text: About a thousand men and women

cards.text: Next Abimelech camps against Thebez and captures it. But inside is a strong tower, and all the men, women and leaders flee there, lock themselves in and climb up to the roof.

cards.question: Abimelech walks right up to the entrance of the tower in Thebez to set it on fire.
Up on the roof of the tower, a woman drops something on Abimelech's head. What is it?

cards.text: His skull is crushed. And Abimelech quickly calls for his armor-bearer.

cards.question: What does Abimelech tell his armor-bearer to do?

answers.text: Draw his sword and kill him
Go and bring Zebul to him

cards.question: Abimelech gives his reason: "lest they say of me, 'A ___ killed him.'"

cards.text: So the armor-bearer runs him through, and Abimelech dies. When the Israelites see it, they all just go home.

cards.question: God repaid Abimelech for the wickedness of murdering his seventy brothers.

cards.text: And the men of Shechem? God brings all their wickedness back upon their own heads.

cards.question: With that, whose curse comes upon the men of Shechem?

findings.problem: Stop 1, card 19 quotes "Go out now and ___ them!", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: Stop 2, card 16 quotes "lest they say of me, 'A ___ killed him.'", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card says the leaders of Shechem put Abimelech on the throne. That fact comes from Judges 9:6, which is outside this passage, but the card cites only Judges 9:22 and gives no reference for it.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Abimelech is named on the opening card without saying who he is, such as Jerubbaal's son who murdered his brothers. Jerubbaal also appears on card 4 with no introduction. The passage starts in the middle of the story, so the baker needs that context.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: "Welcome back, friend" assumes the baker has been here before. Papa Dorin isn't told that, and every baker gets the same lesson.

rule.text: anything about the individual baker that he hasn't been told, such as their streak, their mood, the time of day or how they've done before. In lessons, he's never told, because every baker gets the same lesson.

findings.problem: The wrong answer "It reaches Jotham in Beer first" brings in Jotham, who hasn't been introduced in this walkthrough. A baker meeting the name here for the first time would be confused.

rule.text: The first time someone shows up, he says simply who they are, like "Cyrus, king of Persia" or "Moses, Israel's leader."

findings.problem: The question says "the people of Shechem" cursed Abimelech. The text only says "they," which follows the leaders of Shechem and Gaal. The card names a group the text doesn't name.

rule.text: Leave open what the text leaves open: who is being spoken to, why, or how two things connect.

findings.problem: "In the morning, Gaal goes out" adds a time that Judges 9:35 doesn't give. Only Zebul's plan in 9:33 mentions sunrise.

rule.text: Times stay true. No time in the text means none added.

findings.problem: The card says "Abimelech's company takes its stand." Judges 9:44 says "Abimelech and the companies with him," which is plural.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: After card 1, the stop's story cards (4, 6, 9, 11, 14, 17, 19) are plain summaries with almost none of Papa Dorin's voice. There are no storyteller lines, reactions or personality, even where the moment could hold something respectful.

rule.text: Short, but not stripped down. A story card still has enough of Papa Dorin's voice and enough context that the moment makes sense.
